---
title: "How do I fit a linear regression and explain the slope?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I fit a linear regression and explain the slope?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Decide which variable is the predictor and which is the outcome.

2. Fit lm(y

x).

3. Interpret coefficient units and inspect residuals.

## Runnable example

```{r}
rain_mm <- c(1,2,3,5,6,8,10)
flow <- c(2,4,4,8,11,13,16)
fit <- lm(flow ~ rain_mm)
print(coef(fit))
print(summary(fit)$r.squared)
plot(rain_mm,flow,pch=19,col="#3F78A8",
     xlab="Rainfall (mm)",ylab="Flow index")
abline(fit,col="#A35E20",lty=2,lwd=2)
```

## Interpret the result

The slope represents the modeled change in flow index per additional millimeter of rainfall. It is an association within this model, not a causal claim.

## Check before using real data

A fitted relationship is not automatically causal. Examine residuals and avoid extrapolation.
